name: Rotation curves (SPARC RAR)
data: 175 SPARC galaxies (Lelli+16 rotmod files): observed acceleration V²/R against the baryonic acceleration from the gas, disc and bulge velocities. P4 fitted one disc Υ per galaxy (bulge 1.4Υ) and solved v3's AQUAL law with each galaxy's external field (Chae+21 environments, 109 of 175) and screening at L★ = 24 and 90 pc.
picture: Left and middle: every measured point (small dots) and binned medians (open circles) against v3's law on the canonical and the alt footing (red line), with Newton as the dashed diagonal. Right: the distribution of the fitted per-galaxy Υ on both footings, with the frozen 0.50–0.80 window shaded; P4's Υ grid runs 0.30–1.20, so the piles at the two ends are galaxies sitting on the grid bounds.
why: The points follow the law closely on both footings: the rms scatter is 0.054 dex, well inside the 0.110 line. On the alt footing the larger a₀ makes the fits prefer lighter discs, so the median Υ is 0.44, below the frozen 0.50 window; that splits the tile, so it is conditional. The χ² line fails on both footings (about 63–64 % of galaxies acceptable against 90 %), and the record's kernel ν_mono does the same with the same freedom, so the miss is the error budget or non-circular motions, not something specific to v3. Points are drawn with the isolated law at the file's per-galaxy Υ; the external field changes the rms by under 0.001 dex.

name: Local a0 from MeerKAT
data: 47 MIGHTEE-HI (MeerKAT) galaxies, all deep in the low-acceleration regime, with HI line widths in the rest frame (the frame CFG309 decided); a₀ estimated with the same recipe as 123 SPARC galaxies, using v3's kernel ν₁.
picture: A log a₀ axis. Each row is an estimate with its 68 % (thick) and 95 % (thin) bootstrap interval: MeerKAT rest frame, SPARC same recipe, and the observed-frame variant in grey. The grey band is the ±0.15 dex pass line around SPARC; red lines mark the two footings.
why: The MeerKAT value lands 0.03 dex above SPARC's same-recipe value, far inside the 0.15 dex line, so the tile passes. The observed-frame variant (−0.066 dex) also passes, so the verdict does not hinge on the frame. Both footings sit outside MeerKAT's statistical 95 % interval but inside the recipe's width; the flux-scale systematic is not addressed. No environment estimate exists for these galaxies, so they are treated as isolated.

name: Isolated-galaxy lensing, inner
data: KiDS galaxy–galaxy lensing of isolated blue (late-type) lenses in Brouwer+21's low-acceleration window (g_bar 10^−13.3–10^−11.9 m/s², 6 points), forward-modelled as v3's ΔΣ over the record's 181,477-lens stack.
picture: The amplitude A = data/model (with 2σ_A bars) at each step of the lane's ladder, from the record's algebraic number to the v3 cell (AQUAL, hot CGM, external field), and at the maximum-cluster field. The red line A = 1 means data equal the prediction; 'consistent' is |A − 1| ≤ 2σ_A.
why: Each ingredient of v3 is added one at a time. The kernel, cosmology and forward-modelling barely move A; adding a hot circumgalactic gas halo of half the stellar mass drops it by about 0.11, and the external field moves it by at most 0.004 in this window. On the canonical footing A stays consistent with 1; on the alt footing it is 'between' (−2.9σ) and only becomes consistent at the maximum-cluster field, so the tile is conditional. It hinges on the unmeasured hot gas of blue lenses and on SPS stellar masses, and it holds only for μ_K < 0.1/Mpc (S4); the μ_K²ψ term was not included in S2.

name: Isolated-galaxy lensing, all radii
data: Weak lensing out to 3 Mpc around 2,251 spectroscopically isolated GAMA galaxies (P2), plus S4's test of v3's μ_K²ψ term against Brouwer+21's isolated-lens profile with its released covariance.
picture: Left: the measured excess surface density ΔΣ (multiplied by R so the outer points show) with errors against v3's prediction with no external field (solid red) and with the field the catalogue's own baryons imply (dashed), canonical footing; the alt no-field curve is dash-dot. Right: the largest departure of v3 from the plain law inside 1.1 Mpc as μ_K grows, against the 0.14 guard line.
why: Beyond 1.1 Mpc the stack sits below the zero-field prediction and is consistent with the catalogue-field one, but the two predictions differ by under 1σ with this sample; the frozen line needs 3σ, which needs roughly ten times more lenses, so the tile is undecided. Separately, S4 finds that any μ_K of 0.1/Mpc or more makes v3 depart from the law by more than the guard inside 1.1 Mpc (Δχ² +110 / +190 at 0.1), so the tile can only stay open if μ_K is below that.

name: Tidal dwarfs, NGC 1052-DF2/DF4
data: Six tidal dwarf galaxies (Lelli+15: rotation, baryonic and dynamical masses) and the two ultra-diffuse galaxies NGC 1052-DF2 and DF4 (velocity dispersions), all sitting in their hosts' fields (g_e 0.15–0.28 a₀).
picture: Left: each TDG's measured dynamical-to-baryonic mass ratio (log) with its error; the red line at zero is what dust-free v3 (Newton) predicts. Middle: the mean residual with ±2 se for each reading of v3 — dust-free (U1's own dynamics), posited multi-stream dust, the static AQUAL solution with the host field (P4), and the isolated law. Right: DF2 / DF4 observed σ against dust-free v3 and static AQUAL.
why: Solved as a static AQUAL problem in the host's field, v3 over-predicts these systems: the TDGs sit −0.59 dex below it and DF2/DF4 −1.66 ln below (P4, a fail). U1 then showed from v3's own equations that a system falling freely with its host cannot hold dust (the host's pull on the dust is exactly the external-field term), so v3's own prediction is Newtonian. The data sit on that: TDGs +0.055 ± 0.114 dex, DF2/DF4 +0.30 / −0.24 ln, with no knob. TDG discs have turned less than one orbit, and every estimator assumes equilibrium.

name: Outer globulars: L* floor
data: Line-of-sight velocity dispersions of the distant Milky Way globulars NGC 2419, Pal 4 and Pal 14 (Pal 3 reported), each solved as a Plummer sphere in the Galaxy's field with v3's stiffened field equation; SPS stellar M/L (Υ_V logN(1.6, 0.15 dex)), binary fraction 0.3.
picture: Left: Δχ² against the screening length L★ on both footings, from unscreened AQUAL (left end) to Newton (right end); the red dashed line is the 95 % cut and the dotted verticals the resulting floors. Right: each cluster's own Δχ² (canonical), showing which clusters set the bound.
why: Unscreened AQUAL predicts dispersions well above the measured ones for Pal 4 and Pal 14, so it is excluded in every cell; screening with L★ of about 22 pc or more brings v3 back to the data, and no finite L★ beats Newton, so this is a lower bound only. The floor is set by the M/L prior: with the mass-function-slope M/L (CFG332) the band drops to 3–10 pc and straddles the 20 pc window edge, which is why the tile is conditional.

numbers.what: band over Υ prior and MW field, canonical

name: Central ellipticals (SLUGGS)
data: Globular-cluster velocity dispersions at large radius around four central ellipticals (M87, NGC 4365, NGC 4374, NGC 5846) from SLUGGS, with measured GC density profiles and anisotropy where available (CFG528b), rerun by S4 with v3's kernel ν₁.
picture: Each galaxy's offset between the measured and the v3-predicted dispersion (dex) with ±2σ statistical bars, for the measured-tracer row and for the joint best case (every admissible lever pushed in the law's favour), on both footings. The red line at zero is the law.
why: Three of the four centrals sit well above the law, by 0.09–0.15 dex even in the joint best case; only NGC 4374 is cleared. The class tension is 3.1σ on the less favourable footing (3.3σ if host ownership is dropped, as v3 has no ownership rule). Mass-side levers (IMF, distance, hot gas, external field) cannot remove it; only the unmeasured tracer slope and anisotropy for three of the four could, so the tile stays undecided. The errors are statistical only.

name: Galaxy groups (BFJR)
data: 63 galaxy groups from Tian+2026 (member velocity dispersion, mean projected radius, K-band + X-ray-gas baryonic mass), scored with v3's law on the catalogue baryons with a whole-system aperture.
picture: The mean offset of the groups from v3 (with total error) when the groups are taken as isolated, and when an external field of 0.01 and 0.03 a₀ is solved, on both footings. The grey band is the CONSISTENT zone |Z| < 2.
why: Taken as isolated, the groups sit on the law: +0.010 / −0.010 dex, Z ±0.31, with no supply or edge rule (v3 has none). Every aperture variant stays consistent. The pass depends on the groups' external field, which is not on disk: at 0.01 a₀ they stay consistent (Z 1.94 / 1.46), but at 0.03 a₀, the low end of SPARC environments, they sit above the law (Z 4.7 / 4.5). The baryon masses inherit a Kroupa K-band M/L. The μ_K² term was not included.

name: MW vertical force (round rule)
data: The vertical force K_z at 1.1 kpc above the Galactic plane for 43 mono-abundance populations (Bovy & Rix 2013, with a 5 % error floor), against v3's AQUAL solution for the Milky Way's baryons (McMillan17 and three bracketing baryon models).
picture: Measured K_z against radius (log scale) with errors; the thick red lines are v3 on the canonical (solid) and alt (dashed) footings for McMillan17's baryons, the faint lines are v3 for the other baryon models.
why: The record's pass used a round enclosed-mass rule that v3 does not have. v3's own AQUAL phantom is disc-like, so it adds vertical force where the disc is: K_z at the Sun comes out 92.3 / 96.9 against 66.4 ± 2.2, with a longer scale length than the data. χ² is 178 / 251 against the 67.5 line, and every baryon model fails, as do screening and a 0.03 a₀ field. McMillan17 is partly halo-fitted; the other models bracket that.

numbers.what: K_z(R₀) v3 canonical / alt vs data

name: MW outer slope (Gaia)
data: The Milky Way's circular velocity from Gaia DR3 red giants (Ou+24, 37 points; Jiao+23 in the primary test) over 15–27.5 kpc, against v3's AQUAL disc solution for McMillan17's baryons in the Galaxy's external field.
picture: Left: the measured rotation curve (window points dark, others grey) with the data's slope (dotted) and v3 drawn as a power law with its own fitted slope and V(20 kpc), on both footings. Right: v3's slope as each ingredient is added (kernel, disc geometry, external field), against the data slope band, with the primary Z.
why: The Gaia curve falls steeply beyond 15 kpc (slope −0.325); v3 falls only gently (−0.126 / −0.114), so the shape is excluded at Z −4.37 / −4.62. No ingredient cures it: the kernel, the AQUAL disc solve and the external field each move the slope by about 0.01, and the μ_K² term (first-order bound) makes it shallower still. The cause is the steep DR3 decline itself, not the law's amplitude: at the census baryons v3 also runs low (V(20 kpc) 196.1 / 203.3 km/s), but rescaling the stellar mass to fix the amplitude leaves the slope at -0.147 / -0.126. Cepheids (Feng+26) are shape-consistent. The power-law lines on the left are a drawing aid; the verdict uses the lane's solved curves.
